title: The convergence record, and what a flip would still need
description: Two divergences closed, two remaining and recommended for permanent acceptance. State that honestly in the place the previous spec recorded the original four, and say plainly what a default flip would still require — so nobody reads two closed divergences as a green light.

successCriteria.description: conformance.engines.test.ts pins the divergence set to exactly what a real run now produces, with the per-field records updated to match, and STILL FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — a new divergence and a silently fixed one both break it.

docs/pge-graph.md's engine-migration disposition records which divergences closed in this spec, which remain, and why history and audits are recommended for permanent acceptance rather than left as open work.
oracle-retention.test.ts still asserts pipeline.engine defaults to "ts", that TsPipelineEngine is what the default config selects, and that it is still the fallback. This spec flips nothing.

The document states plainly what a flip would STILL require beyond this spec — at minimum the remaining divergences' disposition, Option B success semantics, a durable checkpoint mechanism for commit and finalize, and an explicit re-specification of the bar itself.
Every claim the document adds is backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true, and `pge docs --check` passes.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green; golden gate passes.

nonGoals: Re-specifying the conformance bar — that is a stated decision, not a sprint.
stopConditions: The divergence set is not what this spec predicted — record what it actually is and why, rather than adjusting anything to match the prediction.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, the golden gate passing, and every documentation claim added backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: This is the spec's closing record and should read like one. The previous spec's disposition section is the model: it stated the outcome, named what was enforced by which test, and said what stayed unproven. Do the same. The most valuable sentence you can write is the one that stops a future reader treating 'two of four closed' as progress toward an automatic flip — the remaining two are recommended for permanent acceptance, which means the bar itself has to change before a flip is possible.
evaluatorNotes: Verify sc-6-1 by mutation in both directions — add a fake divergence and remove a real one, and confirm each fails. Verify sc-6-3 by reading oracle-retention.test.ts and confirming it is unmodified or only strengthened. For sc-6-2 and sc-6-4, check the prose against reality: every divergence it claims closed should be absent from a real harness run you perform yourself.
